response: Yes, socioeconomic status (SES) can significantly impact the learning needs of postpartum women. Women from lower SES backgrounds may face additional challenges, such as limited access to healthcare resources, lower health literacy, and increased stress, which can affect their ability to learn and adapt to postpartum care. In contrast, women from higher SES backgrounds may have greater access to resources, social support, and healthcare services, which can facilitate their learning and adaptation to postpartum care. Therefore, healthcare providers should consider the socioeconomic status of postpartum women when assessing their learning needs and developing individualized education plans.
